key_insight: LLMs can answer many questions correctly while still mishandling missing information under different closure assumptions.
engineering_relevance: AI agents should be tested on whether they apply source-specific rules for missing information, not just reason correctly over recorded facts.
method: Test each base scenario under open-world, closed-world, and local closed-world assumptions, changing only how missing information is treated.
Count a base scenario as correct only when all closure variants are answered correctly.
Extend evaluation to agent action choice, source scope, and updates.
evidence_signal: Across 960 instances and replicated runs, overall accuracy ranged from 71.18% to 99.86%, while core switch accuracy on scenarios whose gold labels change with the closure assumption ranged from 18.23% to 99.31%.
watch_item: Local closed-world assumptions require careful scope handling: some agents answered unknown even when the prompt required treating missing information as false.
paper_title: ClosureBench: A Benchmark for Reasoning under Closure Assumptions
